it-osm-14873744: From Palermo, the old Balarm, a long stretch of asphalt along the coast to Bagheria (a train can skip it).
it-osm-14894235: A gentle climb across the great Battaglietta sinkhole, with a short detour to its swallow hole, the "zubbiu".
it-osm-14894320: A magnificent but demanding walk from the hamlet of Nociazzi near Castellana Sicula.
it-osm-14894646: A trail past the many "màrcati", old shepherds' enclosures of the Madonie.

it-osm-14894767: From Gratteri to Isnello, starting through the park of the Grotta Grattara at the edge of town.
it-osm-14894858: From the Pianetti picnic area above Cefalù through a cork-oak and holm-oak wood to the top of Pizzo Sant'Angelo at 1,080 m.
it-osm-14895034: The Vallone dei Molini, named after its many old watermills, winds through lush vegetation along the Giardinello stream.
it-osm-14895243: Monte San Calogero, the great massif above Termini Imerese, is named after the hermitage of San Calogero, whose ruins lie near the summit.
it-osm-14895300: A more demanding trail from Sclafani Bagni to the Bosco di Favara e della Granza nature reserve.

it-osm-14895494: An old sandstone-paved mule track from near Aliminusa into the Bosco del Cardellino, over the Passo Scacciavalloni.
it-osm-14897640: An old trade and droving route that linked the valley with the main market towns all year round.
it-osm-14899603: Through the Vallone Scopalacqua, with a stop at the spring.
it-osm-15088814: The path winds through the Mediterranean scrub overlooking the coast, it has some ups and downs, the bottom is on limestone rock for a long time and care is required especially if wet, Cala Luna is a little gem to see
it-osm-15342411: An 11 km loop on CAI trails 572 and 573 past the sanctuary of the Cornabusa and Costa Imagna.
it-osm-1534875: A route through 5 protected nature sites, for experienced hikers, with protected passages.
it-osm-15437135: Hike on the Altopiano di Teccu. Start from Bari Sardo, and follow the old Roman Highway up to Teccu.
it-osm-15624873: Part of the trail of the "Teragnole", Trentino women who crossed the Borcola pass from the Val Terragnolo down into the Val Posina.
it-osm-15731930: Leaving Olbia and the wonderful Tavolara behind, up through the Gallura countryside to the lovely little church of San Giacomo.
it-osm-15735159: Through the real Gallura of pastures and granite, to the highest point of the walk, 656 m, on its longest stage.
it-osm-15735328: Giants' tombs and old cork-oak woods lead into historic Tempio Pausania, a pleasure to get lost in among its granite lanes.
it-osm-15736928: Down to the Coghinas valley past pastures, old houses and hot springs, from mountain woods to red volcanic rock.
it-osm-157372: The Keschtnweg leads through chestnut woods, vineyards and villages of South Tyrol, best in autumn at Törggelen time.
it-osm-15867541: A loop through the green countryside and soft hills of Ceresole d'Alba, past the hamlet of Carandi.
it-osm-15952804: Through hazelnut groves and chestnut woods past Braidi, to a view of Tindari with the Aeolian Islands behind.
it-osm-15952850: From Moio Alcantara to Montalbano Elicona, past the Argimusco megaliths, the "Sicilian Stonehenge".
it-osm-15955970: From 1,127 m at the sanctuary of Dinnammare above Messina, with a spectacular view of the Strait and both seas.
it-osm-15956165: Along a forest track through the Vallone di Misitano, under fine pines, oaks, chestnuts and holm oaks.
it-osm-15956197: A hard stage with the longest stretch of asphalt, across the Peloritani ridge to the Tyrrhenian side past the striking Rocca Salvatesta.
it-osm-15956208: A medium stage linking the fine villages of Novara di Sicilia and Basicò.
it-osm-15956319: A medium stage down towards the sanctuary of Tindari, ending on the Coda di Volpe path above the Marinello lagoons.
it-osm-15957012: A hard stage: past the Fiumedinisi stream through the Bosco San Ferdinando.
it-osm-15959864: Through the clay fields of Ceresole d'Alba, past a fish pond and the oak wood of Cascina Bonicelli.
it-osm-15961648: From the hermitage of the Quisquina past the old Byzantine monastery of Melià, a demanding route to the abandoned village of Borgo Riena.
it-osm-15961766: A short, beautiful stage from the hermitage of the Quisquina, with the cave where Santa Rosalia is said to have lived, to Santo Stefano Quisquina.
it-osm-15961880: A variant towards Palazzo Adriano, named after the Montagna delle Rose, once owned by the family of Santa Rosalia.
it-osm-15962167: A varied stage on mountain paths below the ruins of the Gristìa castle, fording the Sosio, then a tiring climb to Chiusa Sclafani.
it-osm-15962373: An easy stage almost all on the old narrow-gauge railway, ending at the pilgrims' refuge in the old Campofiorito station.
it-osm-15962919: A stage through the countryside of Corleone, easy except for the steep climb out of town to the church above Corleone.
it-osm-15962969: At Ficuzza it is worth visiting the Real Casina di Caccia, the royal hunting lodge opened in 1807 for King Ferdinand of Bourbon.
it-osm-15962989: From the slopes of Monte Leardo and Rossella over Portella Sant'Agata to Piana degli Albanesi, Sicily's main Albanian town, famous for its bread and cannoli.

it-osm-15970515: Through Monreale with views over Palermo, then into a forest on good tracks and paths to the end of the stage.
it-osm-15971595: A varied stage through olive groves, pastures and woods with wide views. At Piano Renda, Garibaldi's Thousand camped before taking Palermo.
it-osm-15971714: Most of this stage follows quiet paved lanes, with the Sant'Agata and Rossella farm stays as the only places to eat and sleep below the Portella Sant'Agata pass.
it-osm-15971825: The longest and hardest stage, though without technical sections, passing through two small villages.
it-osm-15971826: One of the most scenic stages, mostly on dirt tracks and paths through the Ficuzza nature reserve.
it-osm-15972001: A stage mostly inside the Ficuzza reserve, on easy dirt roads.
it-osm-15972050: The easiest and one of the shortest stages, mostly downhill: from Marineo into the Eleuterio valley to the Ponte della Fabbrica, built in 1581.
it-osm-15973567: The final stage crosses Piano Stoppa, where the Thousand camped, to Gibilrossa, a spectacular balcony over Palermo with a great obelisk honouring Garibaldi's expedition.
it-osm-15973779: Short-variant stage from Santa Cristina to Marineo; at the bridge over the Eleuterio river you see the striking Cascate delle Sirene waterfalls.
it-osm-16029818: A loop from Bova, one of the most beautiful villages in Italy: from Piazza Roma past the famous steam locomotive 740.054, an old mule track climbs to Monte Grosso for a panoramic view.
it-osm-16112757: A long and tiring route with very steep sections, some ups and downs significantly increasing the elevation gain.
it-osm-162371: Part of the Alta Via della Valle d'Aosta, the high-level hiking route through the Aosta Valley.
it-osm-1635979: A circuit of the Valle Imagna along the watershed, from Almenno San Salvatore to Clanezzo.
it-osm-16381207: The path of the three apparitions of the Virgin Mary "Auspice Maria" at Porzûs.

it-osm-16908125: The stage leaves Terlizzi along the "Route of Churches and Rural Architecture".
it-osm-16908506: The way follows the coast: after a short stop at Santo Spirito it reaches Bari, whose Romanesque basilica keeps the relics of its patron saint Nicholas of Myra.
it-osm-16908585: The way starts in Molfetta, with its beautiful cathedral and ties to Don Tonino Bello, and continues to the centuries-old olive tree of Antignano.
it-osm-16908881: From the Basilica of San Nicola in Bari into the countryside to Capurso, famous for the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Pozzo.
it-osm-16915367: From Rutigliano the route runs through green countryside of ancient olive trees to the lovely town of Conversano.
it-osm-16915740: The stage starts at the church of San Leone in Castellana Grotte and passes through Putignano, known for its carnival.

it-osm-16916058: From Alberobello, through farmland of olive groves and dry-stone walls, to Martina Franca, known for its Baroque architecture and the Valle d'Itria music festival.
it-osm-16916087: The way winds through the Valle d'Itria, full of trulli, dry-stone walls and olive groves typical of rural Apulia.
it-osm-16918732: The way restarts from San Vito dei Normanni, whose square is dominated by the Basilica of Santa Maria della Vittoria, built after the battle of Lepanto.
it-osm-16918863: From Mesagne along the "Messapi di vino" route to San Pietro Vernotico and the Messapian and Roman archaeological site of Valesio-La Pajara.

it-osm-16919430: The route crosses the lush Selva di Supersano woodland, unique on the whole way, to Ruffano, whose mother church is a major monument of Salento Baroque.
it-osm-16919912: From Ruffano to Alessano, the spiritual goal of the way, via Specchia, one of Italy's most beautiful villages, and Tricase, ending at Alessano cemetery where Don Tonino Bello is buried.
it-osm-16920131: The final stage of the Cammino di Don Tonino Bello runs from Alessano to Santa Maria di Leuca and the Sanctuary of Santa Maria de Finibus Terrae.
it-osm-16941683: The first stage starts at the Basilica of Collemaggio in L'Aquila, one of the symbols of Abruzzo.
it-osm-16944256: From Villa Sant'Angelo the stage crosses the Aterno valley to San Demetrio ne' Vestini and, after a climb, joins the Tratturo Magno sheep track.
it-osm-16944367: The stage skirts Castel Camponeschi, climbs the ridge with the cave of San Michele Arcangelo and Bominaco castle, then descends to the Benedictine complex of Bominaco and on to Caporciano.
it-osm-16944395: From Caporciano down to the church of Santa Maria di Cintorelli, through Civitaretenga past Santa Maria in Cerulis to Navelli, one of Italy's most beautiful villages.
it-osm-16944534: From Navelli a deep ravine leads down to the Capestrano plain; along the Tirino river to the magnificent church of San Pietro ad Oratorium and on to Bussi sul Tirino.
it-osm-16945320: From Navelli up to Collepietro, then along the Tratturo Centurelle-Montesecco, with very steep descents, to the ruined church of Santa Maria di Cartignano near Bussi sul Tirino.
it-osm-16945377: From Bussi sul Tirino a steep climb along the Tratturo Centurelle-Montesecco reaches the Rocca Tagliata pass.
it-osm-16946268: From San Clemente, past Torre de' Passeri, up to the entrance of the Majella National Park and the village of Musellaro.
it-osm-16946665: From Salle up to the abandoned village of Salle Vecchio and its castle, down to the Orta river and up the valley to Caramanico Terme, one of Italy's most beautiful villages.
it-osm-16946805: From the Majella Park visitor centre to the bottom of the Orfento valley and the hamlet of Decontra.
it-osm-16947430: From Roccamorice along the Vallone dell'Angelo on the path to the Grotta Sant'Angelo cave hermitage.
it-osm-16948630: From Serramonacesca up to the church of San Liberatore a Majella, along the Alento valley past the ruined Torre di Polegro and the convent of San Francesco Caracciolo to Roccamontepiano.
it-osm-16948739: From Rifugio Di Marco across the Prato della Maiella, past Fonte Carlese, Valle delle Monache and the San Giovanni waterfall, to Guardiagrele, one of Italy's most beautiful villages.
it-osm-16948819: From Roccamontepiano up to Sant'Angelo, then along the foot of the Majella to the Grotta del Colle cave and the village of Rapino.
it-osm-16949152: From Guardiagrele down to Piana San Bartolomeo, the sanctuary of the Madonna della Libera di Filetto and the Franciscan convent of the Annunziata at Feuduccio.
it-osm-16949261: From Orsogna, on the Tratturo Centurelle-Montesecco, down to the Moro stream and along the valley floor towards Lanciano.
it-osm-16950222: From Lanciano up and down through hills to Rocca San Giovanni, one of Italy's most beautiful villages.
it-osm-16950924: From San Giovanni in Venere down to the Adriatic shore, along the coast across the Sangro river and up to the Allied war cemetery.
it-osm-16950961: From the Le Morge trabocco fishing platform along a coastal cycle path, then up through vineyards to the famous Sanctuary of the Madonna dei Miracoli and Casalbordino.
it-osm-16951053: From Casalbordino, below the village of Pollutri and across the Sinello, to Monteodorisio and its Marian sanctuary of the Madonna delle Grazie.
it-osm-16951386: From Monteodorisio through Cupello on constantly rolling hills, then a very steep climb to the village of Lentella, dominated by the church of Santa Maria Assunta.
it-osm-16953052: From Lentella a long descent to the Trigno river, the border between Abruzzo and Molise; after the "Pietra Fracica" ford, a sometimes demanding climb to Montenero di Bisaccia.
it-osm-1696865: A loop around the Taltbühl, said to be the highest wooded hill in Europe in the heart of the Dolomites, to the Schillerhof and the idyllic Totmoos.
it-osm-16978897: Just outside the village is the cave shrine of the Madonna della Bisaccia; further on, the Tratturo Centurelle-Montesecco leads to the next valley and the climb to Guglionesi.
it-osm-16990869: From Guglionesi down to the Biferno river and east between Portocannone and San Martino in Pensilis to Nuova Cliternia and the sanctuary of the Madonna Grande.
it-osm-16990968: From the Madonna Grande back onto the Tratturo Magno to the Saccione stream, the border between Molise and Apulia.
it-osm-16991027: From San Paolo di Civitate past the chapel of the Madonna di Belmonte, then right across wide farmland plains to the town of San Severo.
it-osm-16991112: From Serracapriola down to the Fortore river, where the Taverna di Civitate once stood, a customs post charging tolls to cross the river.
it-osm-16997611: From Apricena to San Marco in Lamis station, then onto the Via Francigena up the flank of the Gargano to the convent-sanctuary of Santa Maria di Stignano.
it-osm-16997612: From San Paolo di Civitate past the drovers' chapel of the Madonna di Belmonte, then left across wide farmland plains to the town of Apricena.
it-osm-16997711: From San Severo along a long disused railway to San Marco in Lamis station, then up the flank of the Gargano to the convent-sanctuary of Santa Maria di Stignano.
it-osm-16997794: From Santa Maria di Stignano a steep, demanding climb onto the Gargano, through an area of rock-cut shrines, then down to the convent of San Matteo Apostolo.
it-osm-16998007: From the convent of San Matteo back up the Gargano on panoramic stretches, then down to San Giovanni Rotondo, the sanctuary where the body of Padre Pio is venerated.
it-osm-16998137: From San Giovanni Rotondo a long climb through woods and open ground to the top of the Gargano and Monte Sant'Angelo, a UNESCO site and the end of the Cammino della Pace.
it-osm-17008248: The fourth stage of the Rotta dei Due Mari runs from Locorotondo to Martina Franca, on the southern Murgia plateau.

it-osm-17162395: The Cammino di San Francesco da Paola is a 318 km, 15-stage pilgrimage and nature route through Calabria, following the footsteps of the Calabrian saint Francis of Paola through the places of his life.
it-osm-17164214: The way is named after the Tabarchini, the people of San Pietro island, home to Carloforte and Calasetta.
it-osm-17191062: Roundtrip part of Via Francigena and Francigena Mare, passing through the cave "Grotta alla Vacca" and the thermal spring "I Bollori".

it-osm-17195155: A round trip to the Grotte di Maurizio caves, the Acquedotto della Forra aqueduct and Poggio alla Forra.
it-osm-17211590: Roundtrip alongside Via Francigena and Francigena Mare, passing through the cave "Grotta alla Vacca", the thermal spring "I Bollori", the cave "Grotta di Maurizio" and the center of Gambassi Terme.
it-osm-17244850: A long stage over the highest ground of the way: the plain known as "Little Tibet", the much-photographed Pietranzoni pond and the striking Scoppaturo canyon, a natural film set.
it-osm-17246950: The second stage of the Cammino del Gran Sasso visits two lovely villages, Castel del Monte and Calascio, and the mysterious Rocca di Calascio castle.
it-osm-17247273: A short, easy stage from Rocca di Calascio to Santo Stefano di Sessanio, full of sights and suitable for families with children.
it-osm-17247876: The final, longer and steeper stage runs from Barisciano past Rifugio Montecristo to Fonte Cerreto, closing the loop of the way.
it-osm-17283705: Starting from the junction with Via Francigena in Via Ponzano in Fucecchio, proceeds to Cerreto Guidi where you will reach the Medici Villa, then continues to Vinci where you can visit the Leonardo Da Vinci Museum.
it-osm-17292999: Second leg from Vinci to Mignana, where where you join the path 10A to Pietramarina, archeological area where in the past was an etruscan fortification.
it-osm-17296770: Third leg from Mignana to the archeological area of Montereggi, on the hill next to Limite, where etruscan remains were found.
it-osm-17298075: In the Middle Ages the "vie romee" were the roads pilgrims took to Rome, which with Jerusalem and Santiago de Compostela was one of the great goals of Western Christendom.
it-osm-1729847: From San Lucio across a meadow and up through the woods to the forest road that climbs to Baita Pianone.
it-osm-17304660: Forth leg from Montereggi archeological area to the Montefortini and Boschetti tumulus in Comeana passing by the archeological museum of Artimino.
it-osm-17309292: From the Sestola riding stables to the church of San Giovanni Battista in Roncoscaglia.
it-osm-17315706: The fifth leg goes towards the centre of Signa where you can visit the Straw Museum. Crossing the Parco dei Renai the path follows the Arno river to reach Parco delle Cascine, the gateway to Florence.
it-osm-17319560: Sixth leg from Ponte all'Indiano, passing through Parco delle Cascine and the historic center of Firenze where there is the National Archaeological Museum.
it-osm-17320823: Last leg from Campo di Marte climbs up to Fiesole, ancient Etruscan city where there is a Civic Archaeological Museum.
it-osm-17324889: First leg starts from Cascine Medicee, continues to the Medici Villa in Poggio a Caiano and arrives in Artimino.
it-osm-17329078: Second leg starts from La Ferdinanda Medici Villa of Artimino, then entering the woods of Montalbano to reach Bacchereto.
it-osm-17332773: The third stage covers both the upper part of Montalbano and its southern slopes and ends in Vinci.
it-osm-17333216: Fourth and last leg that reaches the Medici Villa of Cerreto Guidi and ends in Fucecchio, connecting with the Via Francigena.
it-osm-17336661: The way starts in the main square of Minturno and continues via Solacciano on a road down towards Scauri.
it-osm-17336799: The hardest and most panoramic stage of the way, demanding mainly for its height gain.
it-osm-17336976: From Rifugio Acquaviva to a viewpoint over the Gulf of Gaeta and the Pontine Islands, then onto the old Via della Neve, the ancient snow road.
